edition.notes: The exact electronic-reset PDF identifies the Leonine-recognized Roman Pontifical and contains plural and singular ordination forms. This dated edition controls only its own late nineteenth-century architecture; it is not the 1595 editio princeps, the medieval Pontificale Romano-Germanicum, a manuscript witness, or current liturgical law.
edition.title: Pontificale Romanum, jussu editum a Benedicto XIV et Leone XIII recognitum et castigatum

passages.context: PDF pages 38–39 were inspected through extracted text with the lector ending and acolyte opening as boundaries. The titled section summons and names candidates, places them kneeling before the pontiff, gives an admonition, uses delivery and touch of a liturgical book, and concludes with two prayers before returning the ordinands to their places. This verifies the late nineteenth-century section's ordinal architecture, not its formulas for reproduction, medieval origin, continuity from the PRG, actual practice, frequency, current ministry or law, efficacy, identity with major exorcism, or operational instruction.
passages.notes: No prayer, charge, or operative wording is transcribed. The PDF is an electronic reset whose rasterized pages did not display the text; it is not a manuscript or facsimile witness.

work.author: Catholic Church
work.description: The Roman liturgical book for rites ordinarily celebrated by a bishop, transmitted through materially different editions and reforms. Edition records must identify the promulgating authority, date, title architecture, and textual state; one edition cannot be projected backward onto medieval pontificals or forward into current discipline.
